name: mindplan-mcp

tools.name: run_check
tools.description: Call before in-review, before ship, and before telling the user the work is done. Runs the same check as `mindplan-mcp check`: graph load, exclusivity, coverage, presence (claims, and linked tests once a node is in review or shipped), leftovers, and the import matrix. Returns { ok, output, failures, warnings, info }: output is exactly what the CLI prints (`mindplan-mcp check: ok`, or one Blocked: line per failure with the fix for each illegal import, then Warning: and Info: lines). Warnings flag draft nodes missing required sections (shape:), stale territory text, next-slot imports (one release before they Block), split route families, revisions in review with no linked tests, hotspots (hotspot: a shipped node shipping far more often than the project's median lately, ranked by fan-in, with its recent change groups), fan-out (fan-out: a pre-ship node whose depends_on targets sit in several other unshipped changes, so it may need to know every feature of a kind; invert it onto a Foundation contract, or record keep_whole), and leftover mirror twins from releases before 0.8.0 (upgrade_project removes them), and never fail the check; info lists paths a plan names before building them (planned:), one line per node. A graph that needs setup_project or upgrade_project fails with Blocked: Version. An unclaimed source file is Blocked: Coverage with its probable owner and the claim call. Pass change to also run the in-review gate on every member of that change: its open revisions (shipped nodes with planned edges are listed, not gated), with an additivity: info line and change.additivity (new nodes, reopened shipped nodes with their fan-in). A shipped node with no open next whose claimed files changed against the base gets every stale-text signal. Pass merge before telling the user a PR is ready to merge: it Blocks every node still in review (ship its change, or move it back to in-progress), and with "strict" also in-progress nodes whose claimed files changed against base; results carry merge grouped by change. Moves to in-review and ship run this check on the node's files themselves.

base.description: Opt-in: also enforce dirty-src ownership against this git ref (not used by CI).

change.description: Also check every member of this change (imports, ownership, stale text) and list its members, each with kind revision | planned.

merge.description: Merge gate: true Blocks in-review nodes and Bugs; "strict" also Blocks in-progress nodes whose claimed files changed against base (default: the main/master merge base).

tools.name: get_mindplan_graph
tools.description: Call when you need the graph's nodes and edges, or a slice of them. Prefer orient_for_work for one piece of work. For a question about part of the graph, filter and project instead of reading every node: e.g. state: ["draft", "ready"] with fields: ["id", "type", "title", "change"] and edges: false lists what is planned but not built. state, type, and change combine with AND; values inside one array combine with OR. Returns one page of the MindPlan graph assembled from <id>.mdx frontmatter: nodes sorted by id, the edges whose source is in the page, total_nodes, total_edges, and next_offset while nodes remain, all over the filtered set. edges: false leaves out edges and total_edges; an array (e.g. ["depends_on"]) keeps only those edge types. A graph of up to 200 nodes fits one page; walk offset = next_offset for the rest.

state.description: Only nodes in this state, or in any of these states (e.g. "ready", ["in-progress", "in-review"]). Matches the live state field.

type.description: Only nodes of this type, or of any of these types.

change.description: Only the nodes of this change: an open revision's change id, else a pre-ship node's change field.

fields.description: Node fields to return (id is always included), e.g. ["id", "type", "title", "change"]. Valid: id, type, title, description, state, created_at, updated_at, shipped_at, revisions, split_at, split_into, churn, churn_at, severity, belongs_to, depends_on, exposes, leads_to, mounts, affects, implements, added_claims, tests, aliases, planned, attributed, role, next, rules, change, change_ref, decisions.

edges.description: true (default): every edge whose source is in the page. false: no edges and no total_edges. An array: only edges of those types (OR); total_edges counts them. Valid types: depends_on, belongs_to, exposes, leads_to, affects, mounts.

tools.name: export_mindplan_view
tools.description: Call when a human wants a map for a PR or a doc. Exports a deterministic typed-DAG projection as Mermaid or DOT. Omit focus for the full filtered map; pass focus for that node plus its 1-hop neighborhood. By default hides deprecated/cancelled nodes and closed bugs. Prefer find_related_nodes for agent orientation JSON. A diagram over 80000 characters is Blocked unless you pass focus or output (a repo-relative file path, outside mindplan/).

focus.description: When set, export focus + 1-hop linked neighborhood only.

include_retired.description: Include deprecated/cancelled nodes and closed bugs (resolved/wontfix). Default false.

decisions.description: Label each node that has active decisions with their count. Default false.

output.description: Repo-relative file path to write the diagram to (outside mindplan/). The result then carries written_to and no diagram.

tools.name: find_related_nodes
tools.description: Call before creating a node, to reuse one that already exists. Ranks nodes for a text query (keyword plus semantic search; an exact id ranks first) and returns the focus node plus its 1-hop linked neighborhood (summaries only). Prefer this over get_mindplan_graph for orientation. Provide query and/or node_id. Use get_node_context for full territory; get_blast_radius for transitive dependents.

query.description: Free-text query to rank nodes (keyword and semantic: id, title, description, area, headings, paths). Required if node_id omitted.

node_id.description: Force focus to this node when present. Required if query is empty.

type.description: Optional type filter applied before ranking.

limit.description: Max ranked matches to return (default 5, max 20).

area.description: A Capability id (list_areas): rank only that Capability's Interactions, the Interfaces exposing them, and the Foundations they depend on. Omit for a question that cuts across Capabilities.

tools.name: list_areas
tools.description: Call when you are unsure where work lands, before orient_for_work. Returns every Capability as one row of a compact table: { columns, rows, count } with [id, title, description (60 characters), interactions, interfaces, foundations, open_bugs]. Pick a row and pass its id as area to orient_for_work or find_related_nodes; for a question that cuts across Capabilities, search without area.

tools.name: get_node_implementation
tools.description: Call before editing a file, to see who owns it, or when you need a node's claimed files. Returns declared owned files for a node (`implements`), or looks up the owner of a path. Interaction/Interface/Foundation: { node_id, files: [{path,exists}], next_files? }. Capability/Bug: tagged files of members/affects targets. Pass path for path→owner lookup.

node_id.description: Node id whose implements list to read. Required unless path is set.

path.description: Repo-relative path to look up owner for.

tools.name: get_node_context
tools.description: Call when you are about to read or edit one node's territory. Returns authoritative record (graph slice), editable body (without the ## Rules and ## Decisions sections), the node's own rules, its own decisions (active ones; an empty list may still have superseded history, and a live decision replaced on the open next slot is hidden too: pass include_superseded to see the trail, as in list_decisions), inherited_decisions ({ count, nodes }, plus entries with include_inherited_decisions), resolved_rules (every node rule that reaches it: it counts as orienting on the node), attachment paths, and filenames. Includes next slot when an evolution is in progress (`next.record` + `next.body` + `next.decisions`). Both slots come back unless slot names one; section returns one section of each body.

node_id.description: The id of the node whose territory to read.

include_superseded.description: Also return superseded decisions (each names superseded_by). Default false.

include_inherited_decisions.description: Also return the decisions inherited through belongs_to / depends_on (a Bug: past the nodes it affects): whole at distance 1, one line { id, node_id, distance, decision } beyond. Default false: only their count and nodes.

slot.description: Return only this slot's body (get_node_context: and its decisions): current (live) or next (the open revision; Blocked when none is open).

section.description: Return only this section of each body, e.g. "## Spec"; a missing heading is Blocked and lists the sections. Read a large node a section at a time.

tools.name: orient_for_work
tools.description: Call before each action, after get_rules. Not only at session start. Summary first: with only a query it returns ranked rows ({ id, type, state, title, description, area?, score }, default 8, no body, rules, or decisions); pick one and call again with node_id, or pass change alone to orient on every member of a change in one reply (open revisions, planned sources, and the nodes holding a decision recorded under it as kind "decision"; each member's rules_from, each rule source's text once, the members holding decisions), which clears the write gate for all of them. When the top row is a clear winner (its exact id, the only match, or twice the next score) the full node comes back with the rows and auto_focus: true. With node_id it returns the full node at depth: record and body (get_node_context), owned files, the body being the active slot's (the open next while a revision is open; slot picks one, section cuts it to one section), and at full the 1-hop neighborhood and get_blast_radius for a Foundation, Interaction, or Interface, plus stability ({ fan_in, rate, median_rate, revisions?, split_at?, split_into?, hotspot?, fan_out? }): how many nodes depend on it directly and how often it shipped lately against the project's median; check it before choosing open_next. A pre-ship node's fan_out ({ count, changes }) names the other unshipped changes it depends on; several mean it may need to know every feature of a kind. A full reply carries shape while the node has a transition ahead: the required sections of its active slot, each present, missing, or stub, and the gates that check them. Writes that act on a node (set_implementation_files, set_test_files, update_node_status, patch_node_territory, patch_node_rules, open_next, record_decision, attachments, force_unship, link_nodes / unlink_nodes on the source) are Blocked: Orientation until that node had a full reply in this session (or get_node_context), and again after the rules that reach it changed; create_node is never blocked. Also returns a rules block: the node rules that apply to the focus (its own, its Capability's, its Foundations', or an affected node's for a Bug), each labeled with the node it came from and tagged with a version; pass known_rules_versions ({ node_id: version }) only for entries whose text you still hold, to leave that text out (they come back with unchanged: true). Those rules are mandatory. And a decisions block, at every depth: the focus node's own recorded design decisions (a Bug: those of the nodes it affects), the reply's only copy of them; read them before reshaping that design. inherited_decisions ({ count, nodes }) names the Capabilities and Foundations whose decisions also apply; include_inherited_decisions adds them (whole at distance 1, one line beyond). Superseded ones only with include_superseded. Blast radius groups affected_files by owner and omits cancelled/deprecated by default. Interaction focus also includes reachability (exposing Interfaces, containing Capabilities, leads_to downstream).

query.description: Free-text query to rank nodes. Required if node_id and change are omitted.

node_id.description: Force focus to this node when present.

change.description: Orient on every member of this change (open revisions, planned sources, and nodes holding a decision under it) in one reply; pass it without query or node_id.

limit.description: Max ranked rows (default 8 for a query alone, 5 with node_id).

depth.description: rules: the node's rules and record only. body: also its body. full (default): also the neighborhood and blast radius.

include_superseded.description: Also return superseded decisions in the decisions block (each names superseded_by). Default false.

include_inherited_decisions.description: Also return the decisions inherited through belongs_to / depends_on (a Bug: past the nodes it affects): whole at distance 1, one line { id, node_id, distance, decision } beyond. Default false: only their count and nodes.

known_rules_versions.description: Node id → rules version you already hold (from an earlier rules block); those entries come back without their text, with unchanged: true.

area.description: A Capability id (list_areas): rank only that Capability's Interactions, the Interfaces exposing them, and the Foundations they depend on. Omit for a question that cuts across Capabilities.

slot.description: Return only this slot's body (get_node_context: and its decisions): current (live) or next (the open revision; Blocked when none is open).

section.description: Return only this section of each body, e.g. "## Spec"; a missing heading is Blocked and lists the sections. Read a large node a section at a time.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Call before the first answer or code change in a session, and again after the product description or rules change. Not before every action. Returns the systems dialect and this product's description and standing rules ({ path, description, rules, rules_version, playbook, check, version? }). playbook is the bundled MindPlan dialect; description/rules come from mindplan/project.md. rules_version tags the rules: pass it to get_rules as known_version. version appears only when the graph needs setup or an upgrade, or the server is older than the graph, and names the fix (setup_project, upgrade_project, or the package to install); until then every other graph tool is Blocked.

tools.name: get_spec
tools.description: Call when you need a specific MindPlan rule (lifecycle, required sections, change ids, neighbors, decisions, imports, orientation) instead of guessing or retrying. Returns one part of the running server's own SPEC.md ({ topic, version, text }) by stable topic id, or a tool's SPEC entry by tool name. Without topic it lists the topic ids and tool names.

topic.description: A topic id (e.g. territory-shape, lifecycle, change-ids, neighbors, decisions) or a tool name (e.g. run_check). Omit to list them.

tools.name: get_skill
tools.description: Call when the playbook or the server instructions name a skill, before acting on it. Returns the skill served by this server: { name, text, files } (text is SKILL.md without frontmatter; files are its supporting files). Pass file to read one supporting file ({ name, file, text }). Without name it lists the skills ({ name, description, files }).

name.description: Skill name, e.g. plan-project or define-entities. Omit to list them.

file.description: A supporting file of the skill, as listed in files (e.g. examples.md). Needs name.

tools.name: get_rules
tools.description: Call before each action, before orient_for_work. Returns the mandatory project rules ({ path, rules, rules_version }) from mindplan/project.md. Empty string when the section is empty. While you still hold the rules text, pass its rules_version as known_version: when the rules are unchanged the reply is { path, rules_version, unchanged: true } and that text still applies; otherwise it carries the new text and tag. Without the text in context (a new session, a summarized one), pass nothing. These are the global rules only; node rules arrive through orient_for_work. Does not return the playbook or description.

known_version.description: The rules_version of rules text you still hold (from get_project or get_rules); the text is left out when it still matches. Omit it when you no longer have the text.

tools.name: patch_node_territory
tools.description: Call when a node's title, description, or body should match the work, before the feature code. Required writer for territory prose: body (whole body), section + text (rewrite one ## section), replace { find, with } (one exact edit), toggle_checkboxes, optional title/description/role (pre-ship or open evolution). Prefer section/replace for small fixes: they do not resend the body. Do not edit mindplan/ MDX with host file tools. When a shipped node has an open evolution, patches default to next. Optional slot: current|next. A contract write to a slot in state ready (territory text or checkboxes, claims, links) moves that slot back to draft and returns readiness_reset; self-ready it again after review. change / change_ref set the revision's change id (grouping only: never resets readiness); moving the last revision off a change drops its planned edges (cleared_planned). On a shipped node with no open next both are Blocked: edit its files in place, it needs no change id. aliases replaces the node's search aliases on any node, shipped included, live and an open next alike, without open_next or a readiness reset.

verbose.description: Also return the node's record, its 1-hop neighborhood, and drift. Default false: a write returns { node_id, state, next_state, changed_files }.

aliases.description: Search aliases: synonyms, the words users will say, other languages (e.g. quote, request a quote, ofertă). Replaces the list; [] clears it. At most 20, each up to 60 characters.

body.description: Replace entire territory body below frontmatter.

section.description: Heading of one section to rewrite, e.g. "## Purpose". Needs text. Other sections and the heading line stay as they are.

text.description: Replacement text for the section named by section.

replace.description: Replace one exact piece of the body without resending it.

find.description: Exact text to find in the body (must be unique unless all).

toggle_checkboxes.description: Toggle markdown checkboxes by matching line content. Returns toggled: the lines as written. Close an item honestly with note or not_applicable instead of rewording it.

contains.description: Substring to match on a checkbox line.

checked.description: true for [x], false for [ ]. Optional with note or not_applicable (both tick).

all.description: Toggle every matching line. Without it, a substring matching several lines is Blocked.

note.description: Tick with a note, written as " — note: <text>" after the item.

not_applicable.description: Tick as not applicable with a reason, written as " — n/a: <reason>". Counts as done.

change.description: Set this revision's change id (a slug); empty string clears it. Blocked on a shipped node with no open next.

change_ref.description: Optional branch name or PR URL for the change. Empty string clears it.

slot.description: Territory slot to patch. Defaults to next when an open evolution exists.

split_into.description: Foundation with an open revision only: the Foundations this revision splits out of it. Shipping the revision records the split (split_at, split_into) for those it depends_on, and resets its hotspot rate.

tools.name: patch_node_rules
tools.description: Call when a rule applies to one node and the work that inherits from it, not everywhere (use patch_project_rules for rules that apply everywhere). Replaces the ## Rules section of that node; an empty string clears it. Works on any non-retired node, including shipped ones, without open_next. Returns rules_impact: the nodes whose work the rules reach.

rules.description: Replace the node's ## Rules section. Empty string clears it. No level-1 or level-2 headings.

tools.name: record_decision
tools.description: Call when you choose between viable designs (a data shape, an ordering guarantee, which system owns a fact), on the node the choice shapes. Appends a structured entry to that node's ## Decisions section: on its next slot while a revision is open, else live. Records are never rewritten: to change a decision, record a new one with supersedes (the old one stays listable as superseded). A decision-worthy revision (a shipped Foundation's contract, a new migration or schema file, a wide blast radius, a depends_on change) is Blocked at in-review until a decision is recorded under its change id or on the node. Never resets readiness.

verbose.description: Also return the node's record, its 1-hop neighborhood, and drift. Default false: a write returns { node_id, state, next_state, changed_files }.

node_id.description: Node the decision shapes (not a Bug).

alternatives.description: What else was considered, one line each (the alternative you rejected, and why it lost).

why.description: The constraint or trade-off that decided it.

consequences.description: What this makes harder or forbids.

keep_whole.description: The node stays one node on purpose (e.g. auth): hotspot detection skips it until this decision is superseded.

supersedes.description: Id of an active decision on this node, its Capability, or its Foundations that this one replaces.

change.description: Change id to record it under (default: the node's open revision's change). It tags the decision only: the node's own change id is never set, so a decision alone does not make a shipped node a member of the change.

id.description: Stable id, e.g. d-capacity-on-booking. Generated from the decision when omitted.

tools.name: list_decisions
tools.description: Call before reshaping a design someone else chose, or to read the reasoning trail of a node or change. Returns { decisions, count }: one node's own decisions, every decision recorded under a change, or the whole graph's, each with its node, status (active or superseded), and superseded_by. Superseded entries only with include_superseded.

change.description: List decisions recorded under this change id.

include_superseded.description: Also return superseded decisions. Default false.

tools.name: patch_project_description
tools.description: Call when the product summary changes. The next session start calls get_project again. Writes the ## Description section of mindplan/project.md via the territory store. Leaves ## Rules unchanged. Do not hand-edit project.md.

description.description: Replace the ## Description section body. Empty string clears it.

tools.name: patch_project_rules
tools.description: Call when standing rules change. The next action calls get_rules again. Writes the ## Rules section of mindplan/project.md via the territory store. Leaves ## Description unchanged. Do not hand-edit project.md.

rules.description: Replace the ## Rules section body. Empty string clears it.

tools.name: patch_config
tools.description: Call when source roots, exclude paths, decision-gate settings, hotspot thresholds, the fan-out threshold, or search settings change. Writes mindplan/config.json sources, exclude, decisions, hotspots, fan_out, and/or search via the territory store. Do not hand-edit config.json.

sources.description: Glob list for the ownership universe (replaces sources when set).

exclude.description: Glob list excluded from the universe (replaces exclude when set).

decisions.description: Decision-gate settings. A field not passed keeps its stored value.

blast_radius.description: A revision with more dependents than this is decision-worthy (default 5).

schema_files.description: Globs of migration and schema files; claiming a new one is decision-worthy.

hotspots.description: Hotspot settings, used by run_check warnings and the open_next warning. A field not passed keeps its stored value.

half_life_days.description: Days for a node's recent ship rate to fade by half (default 30).

outlier_ratio.description: A node shipping this many times as often as the graph's median node is a hotspot (default 3).

min_rate.description: The lowest recent ship rate that can be a hotspot (default 2).

fan_out.description: Fan-out settings, used by run_check warnings. A field not passed keeps its stored value.

warn_at.description: A pre-ship node depending on nodes in this many other unshipped changes gets a fan-out: warning (default 3).

search.description: Search settings. A field not passed keeps its stored value.

enabled.description: false turns semantic ranking off (keyword ranking always runs). Default true.

model.description: Embedding model id (default "Xenova/bge-small-en-v1.5"); changing it rebuilds the search cache.

tools.name: put_attachment
tools.description: Call when a supporting file should sit beside a node. Writes a file under attachments/ (or next-attachments/ while evolving) as base64. Slot defaults to next when an open evolution exists.

verbose.description: Also return the node's record, its 1-hop neighborhood, and drift. Default false: a write returns { node_id, state, next_state, changed_files }.

tools.name: remove_attachment
tools.description: Call when a supporting file should leave a node. Deletes a file under attachments/ (or next-attachments/ while evolving). Slot defaults to next when an open evolution exists.

verbose.description: Also return the node's record, its 1-hop neighborhood, and drift. Default false: a write returns { node_id, state, next_state, changed_files }.

tools.name: set_implementation_files
tools.description: Call before writing a file the node does not yet claim. Replaces the server-owned implements list for an Interaction, Interface, or Foundation. Pre-ship writes current; shipped with an open next writes next; shipped with no open next writes live in place, additive only: every old entry kept (or under a new dir entry), each new entry an exact file (or F/) in a folder F the node dominates (it already claims a file directly in F, no other node claims under F); removing, moving, globbing, claiming elsewhere, or claiming a migration or schema file (config decisions.schema_files) is Blocked → open_next. In-place results list added_in_place; name each in the body with patch_node_territory (run_check warns until then). retired nodes may only shrink. Rejects bad paths and ownership conflicts. Results may carry folder_claims: a folder/ entry that would replace several per-file entries. Entries are files, directories ending in /, or globs (* ** ?; [ ] stay literal), e.g. src/templates/*/actions/i-read-post/. attributed names files a revision adds in another node's claimed folder (a migration in a composition root's single migrations folder): ownership stays with that node, but the decision gate and the blast radius count them for this revision; each must be an exact file another active node claims, and a shipped node needs an open next. A contract write to a slot in state ready (territory text or checkboxes, claims, links) moves that slot back to draft and returns readiness_reset; self-ready it again after review.

verbose.description: Also return the node's record, its 1-hop neighborhood, and drift. Default false: a write returns { node_id, state, next_state, changed_files }.

node_id.description: Pipeline node whose implements list to replace.

files.description: Repo-relative POSIX paths (files, or directories ending in /). Replaces the slot list. Omit with attributed to keep the claims.

attributed.description: Exact repo-relative files this revision adds in another node's claimed folder. Replaces the list; [] clears it.

slot.description: Optional slot override. Defaults by lifecycle.

change.description: Change id for the written slot; empty string clears it. Blocked on a shipped node with no open next (edit its files in place; it needs no change id).

tools.name: set_test_files
tools.description: Call when tests that verify a node exist, before moving it to in-review. Replaces the node's linked tests list for an Interaction, Interface, or Foundation. The list is evidence, not a claim: it does not own the files (claim them with set_implementation_files), several nodes may list one file, and it is written to live and an open next alike, so a shipped node needs no open_next and readiness is never reset. run_check Blocks an entry missing on disk once the node is in review or shipped, and warns about a revision in review with none. get_blast_radius lists the linked tests a change should run. Entries are files, directories ending in /, or globs (* ** ?). An empty list removes it.

verbose.description: Also return the node's record, its 1-hop neighborhood, and drift. Default false: a write returns { node_id, state, next_state, changed_files }.

node_id.description: Pipeline node whose linked tests to replace.

files.description: Repo-relative POSIX test paths (files, directories ending in /, or globs). Replaces the list.

change.description: Change id for the active slot; empty string clears it. Blocked on a shipped node with no open next (edit its files in place; it needs no change id).

tools.name: create_node
tools.description: Call when reuse found no node, before any new-feature code. Creates a Capability, Interaction, Interface, Foundation, or Bug: scaffolds territory folder + <id>.mdx frontmatter. Foundations require role. Declare owned files later with set_implementation_files (no package scaffold). Returns shape for a Foundation, Interaction, Interface, or Bug: the sections its first transition checks, each present, missing, or stub (the scaffold), so you write them before moving it.

verbose.description: Also return the node's record, its 1-hop neighborhood, and drift. Default false: a write returns { node_id, state, next_state, changed_files }.

id.description: Unique slug id for the node, e.g. bug-checkout-race.

role.description: Required for Foundation: assembler | infra | design-system | adapter.

change.description: Optional change id (a slug) that ties this new Foundation, Interaction, or Interface to other revisions of one change.

change_ref.description: Optional branch name or PR URL for the change. Empty string clears it.

aliases.description: Search aliases: synonyms, the words users will say, other languages (e.g. quote, request a quote, ofertă). Replaces the list; [] clears it. At most 20, each up to 60 characters.

tools.name: link_nodes
tools.description: Call when two existing nodes should be connected. Adds an edge to the DAG. Legal shapes: Interaction -belongs_to-> Capability, Interaction|Interface -depends_on-> Foundation, Foundation -depends_on-> Foundation, Interface -exposes-> Interaction, Foundation -mounts-> Interface (a composition root that imports Interfaces), Interaction -leads_to-> Interaction, Bug -affects-> Interaction|Interface|Foundation. While a node has <id>.next.mdx, belongs_to/depends_on/exposes/leads_to writes go to the next slot (proposed edges applied on ship). Pass change on a shipped node with no open revision of that change to plan the edge instead: it is checked like a link (shape, cycles), recorded under the change on the live file without open_next, listed by run_check and get_blast_radius for the change, applied to the next slot when open_next opens the node with that change, and dropped if the change closes first. The live graph does not change. A contract write to a slot in state ready (territory text or checkboxes, claims, links) moves that slot back to draft and returns readiness_reset; self-ready it again after review.

verbose.description: Also return the node's record, its 1-hop neighborhood, and drift. Default false: a write returns { node_id, state, next_state, changed_files }.

source_id.description: The id of the edge source node.

target_id.description: The id of the edge target node.

edge_type.description: belongs_to | depends_on | exposes | leads_to | affects | mounts

change.description: Plan the edge under this change id when the source is shipped and has no open revision of it.

tools.name: open_next
tools.description: Call when a shipped node's contract changes, before editing that contract. Writes <id>.next.mdx from the live file in state draft (a shipped node has no next file until then). Optional title/description overrides. The next file gets a fresh list of unticked default Atomic Ops to rewrite (a shipped node keeps none). The live node keeps serving. Ship from next in-review to promote it over the live file; discard_next to abandon it. Both delete the next file. Pass change to tie this revision to the others of one change (update_node_status scope change, get_blast_radius change, run_check change act on the group). Edges planned on the node under the revision's change are added to the next slot (applied_planned). On a hotspot (a node shipping far more often than the graph's median lately; config hotspots) the result also carries warnings and decision_prompt: prefer a new node that depends_on it, or record why revising it is right.

verbose.description: Also return the node's record, its 1-hop neighborhood, and drift. Default false: a write returns { node_id, state, next_state, changed_files }.

node_id.description: Id of the shipped Foundation, Interaction, or Interface to evolve.

title.description: Optional new title for the next slot.

description.description: Optional new description for the next slot.

change.description: Optional change id (a slug) grouping this revision with others.

change_ref.description: Optional branch name or PR URL for the change. Empty string clears it.

tools.name: discard_next
tools.description: Call when an open evolution should be abandoned. Abandons an in-flight evolution: deletes <id>.next.mdx and next-attachments/. The live <id>.mdx is unchanged. When it was its change's last open revision, the change's planned edges are dropped (cleared_planned).

verbose.description: Also return the node's record, its 1-hop neighborhood, and drift. Default false: a write returns { node_id, state, next_state, changed_files }.

node_id.description: Id of the node whose open evolution to discard.

tools.name: get_blast_radius
tools.description: Call before changing a shipped node. Returns nodes that depend on the given node (transitive reverse depends_on closure), with hop distance, capabilities_at_risk, and affected_files grouped by owner ({ owner_id, owner_type, via[], files[] }; via ∈ focus|dependent|exposing|importer). Cancelled and deprecated nodes are omitted by default; set include_retired to see them (BFS still traverses through retired nodes so live dependents keep true distances). When the focus is an Interaction, also returns reachability. decisions lists the active decisions held by the focus; dependent_decisions ({ count, nodes }) names the dependents that hold decisions a change would reach, and include_dependent_decisions adds their one-line entries to decisions. tests lists the linked test files of the focus and every owner in affected_files: the suites to run. Pass change instead of node_id for the merged radius of every member of a change (open revisions and shipped nodes with planned edges; members carry kind revision | planned), its planned_edges, and additivity ({ summary, new_nodes, revised, planned }): whether the change only adds nodes or reopens shipped ones, each with its fan-in.

node_id.description: The id of the node whose dependents to analyze. Or pass change.

change.description: A change id: merge the blast radius of all its open revisions and planned sources.

include_dependent_decisions.description: Also list the dependents' decisions in decisions (default false: only their count and nodes).

tools.name: unlink_nodes
tools.description: Call when an existing edge should go away. Removes edge(s) between two nodes from the source node's frontmatter. With change, removes only the edges planned under that change from source to target. A contract write to a slot in state ready (territory text or checkboxes, claims, links) moves that slot back to draft and returns readiness_reset; self-ready it again after review.

verbose.description: Also return the node's record, its 1-hop neighborhood, and drift. Default false: a write returns { node_id, state, next_state, changed_files }.

source_id.description: The id of the edge source node.

target_id.description: The id of the edge target node.

change.description: Remove the edges planned under this change instead of real edges.

tools.name: update_node_status
tools.description: Call when a node should move along the build or bug pipeline, including ship or resolved at handoff. Transitions a Foundation, Interaction, Interface, or Bug. Build pipeline: draft -> ready -> in-progress -> in-review -> ship (sets stable/unstable). Bug pipeline: open -> triaged -> fixing -> in-review -> resolved | wontfix. When an open evolution exists, build-pipeline transitions apply to the next slot; ship promotes next over current and deletes the next file; every ship drops the node's Atomic Ops (the shipped node shows its current state, git keeps the ledger). Pass revisions to advance a set in one call: Foundations, then Interactions, then Interfaces, then Bugs; stops on the first Blocked and leaves earlier nodes transitioned. Pass scope + new_status to walk every open update (or a node and its dependents, or one change's revisions) to a target in one call, validated before the first write; dry_run lists every transition. A scoped walk to ship that would skip a node's in-review stop is Blocked unless skip_review: true, which walks it through in-review (gate included) and reports skipped_review. Moves to in-review and ship run the check's import and ownership rules on the node's files and return Blocked: on a violation; stale-text warnings ride along. A move to in-review of a decision-worthy revision (a shipped Foundation's contract, a new migration or schema file, a wide blast radius, or a depends_on change) with no decision recorded is Blocked: Decision with the record_decision call. A Blocked: Orientation names every unoriented node of the call at once (a scope change walk names orient_for_work({ change })). A batch returns one line per node. When a ship or cancel leaves a change with no open revisions, its planned edges are dropped (cleared_planned); scope change walks the change's open revisions. Capability and production stable/unstable are computed automatically.

verbose.description: Also return the node's record, its 1-hop neighborhood, and drift. Default false: a write returns { node_id, state, next_state, changed_files }.

node_id.description: The id of the single node to transition. Mutually exclusive with revisions.

new_status.description: Foundation/Interaction/Interface: draft | ready | in-progress | in-review | ship | cancelled | deprecated. Bug: open | triaged | fixing | in-review | resolved | wontfix. From stable/unstable: deprecated only (or open_next then build/ship next). Pre-ship abandon: cancelled from draft|ready|in-progress|in-review. Required with node_id. Omit when using revisions.

scope.description: Walk many nodes in one call to the new_status target: all_open_updates (every shipped node with an open next, and every pre-ship node being built: in-progress or in-review; draft and ready plans are never walked) or node_and_dependents (node_id plus its open dependents), or change (every open revision with that change id, draft and ready included). The server orders Foundations, Interactions, Interfaces, walks each node through the pipeline, and validates the whole walk before writing anything. Target: ready | in-progress | in-review | ship.

change.description: The change id walked by scope "change".

skip_review.description: Scoped walk to ship only: allow moving nodes that are not in-review yet. Each still passes the in-review gate; the result lists skipped_review.

dry_run.description: Validate and return the plan and the first Blocked reason without writing anything.

revisions.description: One revision. Server orders Foundations, Interactions, Interfaces, then Bugs, and stops on the first Blocked. Mutually exclusive with node_id and new_status.

tools.name: force_unship
tools.description: Call only after the user confirms a mistaken ship; recovery only. Reverses a mistaken Foundation/Interaction/Interface ship: clears shipped_at and sets a pre-ship state (default ready). Requires confirm exactly equal to "unship:<node_id>"; do not invent the confirm token. Blocked while an open evolution exists or shipped dependents exist. Deletes any next file and clears added_claims.

verbose.description: Also return the node's record, its 1-hop neighborhood, and drift. Default false: a write returns { node_id, state, next_state, changed_files }.

node_id.description: Stable/unstable Foundation, Interaction, or Interface to unship.

confirm.description: Exact token after user confirmation: "unship:<node_id>". Do not invent this.

tools.name: setup_project
tools.description: Call when get_project's version or a Blocked: Version names setup_project (the repo has no mindplan/ graph), or the user asks to set up MindPlan. Creates the graph (mindplan/ tree, default config.json, empty project.md, version stamp) and returns { created, changed_files, ci?, pointer, guide }: pointer is the text for MINDPLAN.md, guide the steps that follow (wire CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md, ignores, move rules into the brief with the user's approval, the description, run_check). It writes no other file of yours; on a graph that already exists it writes nothing and returns the guide again. Pass ci: "github" once the user wants the merge-gate workflow (.github/workflows/mindplan-merge-gate.yml; an existing one is kept). Blocked on a graph that needs upgrade_project, or on one newer than this server.

ci.description: Also write the GitHub merge-gate workflow, which runs check --merge on pull requests to the default branch.

tools.name: upgrade_project
tools.description: Call when get_project's version, a Blocked: Version, or the check names upgrade_project: the graph is behind this server, and every other graph tool is Blocked until it is upgraded. Runs every migration (each is idempotent), stamps mindplan/version.json with this server's migration level, and returns { from_level, to_level, changed_files, migrations, leftovers, pointer_outdated, pointer, guide }: leftovers are agent files older releases installed outside mindplan/ (delete them), pointer_outdated says MINDPLAN.md or the agent files need the pointer text, and guide lists the steps. Commit the upgrade on its own. Blocked without a graph (call setup_project) or when the graph is newer than this server.

instructions: Before answering any questions or writing any code for this project, call get_project and read the response. Follow the playbook (systems dialect) and the project description and rules it returns. Project rules are mandatory: before each action, call get_rules then orient_for_work. Before any new-feature code change, update or create the matching nodes using the plan-project skill (load it with get_skill): it covers every graph write (create_node, open_next, discard_next, link_nodes, unlink_nodes, patch_node_territory, patch_node_rules, patch_project_description, patch_project_rules, patch_config, and attachments).
